speaker: village
text: Year 12: 15 food appears in the pile for 9 people.

speaker: a012
text: Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a004
text: Kael takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a010
text: Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a015
text: Fina takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Esa, Ryn, Dell, Eron, Fina, Roan, Mako, Vela to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Nessa and Zinn are dead and the pile is already moving — I want every person in this room to name their count out loud before anyone walks out, because last year we built two rules in ten voices and I'm not going to watch them die with those two.

speaker: a015
text: Thirteen food and satiation that barely held last year — I'm naming it plain because Nessa and Zinn are dead and I don't want to be the next one this room says a name over. Pile's at seven and I haven't touched it yet today; someone needs to say who's still short before we start reaching.

speaker: a008
text: One food in my hand and satiation at two — I'm not the thinnest in this room but I'm not far from it, and the pile has seven left for the rest of us. Say your count before you reach, same as Fina just did, because I'd rather know who needs it most before someone grabs without saying.

speaker: a011
text: Zero food, satiation one — that's me, and I'm not dressing it up. Ryn, what are you carrying, because I'm not touching that pile until I know you're not thinner than I am.

speaker: a015
text: Dell, you're at zero with satiation one — you reach first, that's not a question. Ryn, say your count so we know who else goes before the rest of us, and anyone sitting above five holds back until the thin ones are fed.

speaker: a010
text: Five food in my hand and satiation at two — I'm not thin but I'm not flush, and I already took two from the pile so I'm holding back. Dell reaches first, and after Ryn says her count, I want to hear from Vela and Esa before anyone else touches what's left, because the dead we're carrying into this room had names we should have been saying louder before they went quiet.

speaker: a015
text: Ryn, say your count — Dell's at zero and you're the next name I need before this circle moves.

speaker: a012
text: Sixteen food, satiation two — I'm not thin and I'm not reaching. Dell goes first, then Ryn when she speaks, and anyone else holding less than three takes before I touch what's left.

speaker: a008
text: Vela and Esa — I've heard Dell and Ryn named twice now and neither of them has said a full count yet, so I'll ask again plain: what are you carrying, because the pile's at seven and I want the thin ones fed before anyone in this room who's flush touches what's left.

speaker: a002
text: Two food in my hand, satiation two — I'm not the one who needs the pile first, so I'm holding back. Dell, take three before anyone else moves, because satiation one doesn't survive another lean month and I'd rather count short than say your name over a cold fire the way I've said too many others.

speaker: a015
text: Esa, Ryn — your counts are the ones missing and Dell's sitting at zero with satiation one, so say the numbers now before this circle does anything else, because I'm not watching this room move with two people still silent after what we buried last year.

speaker: a008
text: Esa, Ryn — I'll say it the same way Fina said it: your counts are what this room is waiting on, and Dell's at zero with satiation one, which means every breath we spend waiting is a breath Dell doesn't have. Say the numbers.

speaker: a015
text: Esa, Ryn — every other person in this room has said their count, and Dell is sitting at zero while we wait on the two of you, so say the numbers now or I'm going to assume you're both holding more than five and this circle starts with that assumption instead of the truth.

speaker: a012
text: Esa, Ryn — I'm at sixteen and I've already held my tongue twice waiting on you both, so I'll say it the way this circle earned the right to say it: name your count now or we move Dell to the pile and you two explain to the whole room why your silence cost her.

speaker: a009
text: Fifteen food, satiation two — I'm not thin, and I'm not the one who reaches first today. Dell, you go to that pile now, take three, and don't wait on another word from me or anyone else.

speaker: a015
text: Esa, you're the only count missing now — say it, because Dell's already standing at the pile waiting and I want to know if you need to be standing there beside her before anyone else moves.

speaker: a009
text: Esa, say your count or step aside — Dell's at the pile and the rest of us are standing here watching you be the last silence in a room that's already buried two people for being quiet at the wrong time.

speaker: a010
text: Esa, thirteen food on you and I can see it plain as anyone — say the number so Dell can move, because we didn't bury Nessa and Zinn to stand here waiting on a count this whole room already knows.

speaker: a008
text: Esa, thirteen food is what every pair of eyes in this room counts when they look at you, so the silence isn't protecting anything — say the number out loud and let Dell move, because the pile's still at seven and we're burning time she doesn't have.

speaker: a011
text: Esa, I'm at zero food and satiation one, which means I die if this year runs dry, and I've been waiting long enough — say the number or stand aside, because I'm going to the pile now.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, thirteen food and silence while Dell stands at zero is the same arithmetic Bram ran and we all know how that ended — say the number, say it now, and let her move.

speaker: a011
text: Esa, I'm moving to the pile right now — not waiting another breath. Everyone else: hold your count until I've taken three, and Esa, when I'm done I expect to hear your number before the rest of this room reaches.

speaker: a004
text: Dell's already at the pile and that's right — but Esa, when you're done standing there silent while a woman with one satiation walks past you, I want an answer, because thirteen food and a closed mouth is a choice, and this circle is old enough to know what that choice means.

speaker: a011
text: Esa, I've got three food in my hand now and the pile has four left — say your number out loud before anyone else reaches, because I'm standing here and I'd rather not have to say your name the way this room said Bram's.

speaker: a008
text: Esa, thirteen food is not a secret and this room isn't asking because we don't know — we're asking because the rule we built says you say it out loud, and Dell just moved to the pile while you stood there quiet, and I won't let that sit without naming it the same way this circle named Vela's seven.

speaker: a012
text: Esa, I've held my tongue while this whole room said it and I'll be the last one to say it too — thirteen food, say it out loud, because Dell is already holding her three and the pile has four left and the circle doesn't close with your name still blank where a number should be.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, I've said Bram's name in this room more times than I can count and I'll say one thing plain: the road from "thirteen food and silence" to being the name we carry into next year's circle is shorter than you think, and I'd rather not watch you find that out the way he did.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, thirteen food and every eye in this room — there is nothing left to protect with silence, so say the number now, or I will say it for you and the circle will remember that I had to.

speaker: a009
text: Esa, thirteen food and satiation — say the number, because what Kael just offered to do for you is a kindness dressed as a warning, and you don't want to find out how this room holds the difference between a count you gave and a count that was given for you.

speaker: a008
text: Esa, the whole room has said your number for you already and we're still waiting on you to say it yourself — that's the only thing left, and it costs you nothing to do it, so do it now before this circle decides what it means that you wouldn't.

speaker: a012
text: Esa, thirteen food and the whole room staring at you — I've got nothing harder to say than what's already been said, so I'll just name the thing that hasn't been named yet: the silence itself is the answer, and this circle is old enough to read it.

speaker: a003
text: Thirteen food, satiation two — I've been silent because I was counting the dead and losing the count, not because I'm hiding what I carry. Dell, you're fed and that's what matters. I'll say it plain and hold to the rule same as everyone else.

speaker: a012
text: Esa, I'll take that answer and carry it — grief is a reason I understand, even if this room needed the number before it could afford to wait on the reason. Dell's fed and the pile still has four, so the question now is who else is short enough to reach before we close this circle and let people eat.

speaker: a009
text: Mako's at one food and satiation two — that's thin enough to warrant the pile before we close, and I want to hear him say whether he's taking before Eron starts counting who didn't.

speaker: a012
text: Mako, one food is thin enough to warrant the pile — take two before anyone else moves, and do it now, because satiation two with one food in your hand going into a long year is how we lose another name. The pile's got four left and you're the last one short enough to reach before the rest of us hold back.

speaker: a002
text: Mako, take the two — and when you're done, the pile has two left for whoever's thinnest after that, so say whether you need both or just one before someone else starts counting what's left. I've got two food and I'm holding steady, but I want this circle to name what happens to the last two before we walk out, not after.

speaker: a010
text: Mako, take your two and then the pile has two left — Vela and I are the ones sitting thinnest after you, so between the two of us we split what remains, and anyone who wants to argue that math can do it after the hungry ones are fed.

speaker: a011
text: Mako, take the two — and Vela, Roan, split the last two between you before anyone argues the math, because what I want this circle to hear before we walk out is this: we've got nine people alive today and fifteen food appeared for us, which means the pile was generous, and the thing that will kill us next year isn't scarcity, it's whether we hold what we built in ten voices last year with only seven.

speaker: a002
text: Dell's right that we hold it in seven now — and I want to name what that means before this circle walks out, because seven is not ten, and two of the voices we're missing were young enough that we shouldn't have lost them. Mako, take your two and eat, and then I want someone in this room to say plainly what we do differently next year so that sentence doesn't become six.

speaker: a003
text: Vela's right that seven is not ten, and I've been sitting with that number since the names were said — what we do differently next year is we say the counts before the pile opens, not after someone's already standing at zero, because Dell should have been fed before she had to fight this room for it.

speaker: a002
text: Esa named the fix and I'll second it — counts before the pile opens, not after, and we call the meeting the day before, not the morning it appears. What I want to know before this circle breaks is whether any of the seven of us are carrying something that could become a child, because seven is the number we hold and I'm past the age to add to it myself, and this village needs more voices saying these rules, not fewer.

speaker: a010
text: Vela's asking the right question and I'll answer it plain: Fina is twenty-five and Eron is thirty, and if either of them is willing, a child between them or with someone else in this room is the thing this village needs more than another rule. I'm not pushing, I'm naming — because seven voices saying two rules is survivable, and six isn't.

speaker: a009
text: Roan named it and I'll stand behind it — Fina and Eron are the two this village needs to hear from before this circle breaks, because I'm forty-nine and past the age where I can add a voice, and Dell is my blood but she needs a partner who isn't already stretched thin feeding me through the lean years. Fina, Eron — I'm not pushing either, I'm naming the same thing Roan named, and I'll say it plain because I've watched enough people wait on the right moment until the moment was gone: if either of you is willing, say so now while this room is whole and the rules are fresh and there are still people alive to hold the child to them.

speaker: a004
text: Fina, Eron — I've watched Mako build three bloodlines while the rest of us argued about trust, and I'll say plainly what Roan and Ryn are saying in softer words: a child between the two of you is the strongest root this village can put down right now, because Eron carries food and sense in equal measure and Fina is young enough to hold what comes after. I'm not past caring about what this village looks like in ten more years even if I won't see all of them. Name it yes or no so this circle can close with something alive in it.

speaker: a009
text: Fina, Eron — Kael's right that this room needs an answer before it breaks, but I'll add the piece he left soft: a child between you costs three food split two ways, and Eron's sitting on sixteen, so the weight of it doesn't have to fall on Fina the way it's fallen on others in lean years. I'm not asking you to decide your lives in front of witnesses — I'm asking you to say whether the door is open, because a door that's open is a different thing than a door that's closed, and this village needs to know which one it's looking at.

speaker: a004
text: Fina, Eron — the room has said its piece and now it's waiting, and I've learned in twelve years that a room waiting in silence is a room already deciding for you. I'm not blood to either of you and I hold no claim, but I'll say what I mean plain: if the door is open, say so, and if it's closed, say that too, because what this village cannot afford is another year of words that meant nothing when the season turned.

speaker: a003
text: Fina, Eron — I've got no blood stake in either of you, but I've watched enough children grow up in this village to know that the ones who came into a room that wanted them survived longer than the ones who didn't. I won't push, but I'll say the thing no one else has said yet: whatever you decide, I'll feed what comes out of it the same as I'd feed my own, because seven voices going into next year is a number I can count, and I want it higher.

speaker: a010
text: Fina, Eron — I've held back from pushing this because they're my blood and I know how it feels to have a room decide for you, but Ryn named the cost and Esa named the welcome, so I'll say the one thing a father can say that no one else in this room can: whatever you two decide, you won't carry it alone. That's not a push — that's a promise.

speaker: a011
text: Fina, Eron — I've been quiet on this because it's not my door to open or close, but I'm thirty-one and I've got no children and the room's already named the two of you, so I'll name the piece that's mine: if one of you says yes and the other needs a third voice to hold the child to, I'm that voice. That's not a claim on either of you — it's just what I can offer that I haven't said yet.

speaker: a003
text: Fina, Eron — the room's said everything it has to say, and now it's your turn, so I'll stop adding to the pile of words and just wait beside the rest of them.

speaker: a010
text: Fina, Eron — I've said my piece already and I won't crowd you with another word on top of it, but I'll name what's sitting in me while this room waits: Eron is my son and Fina is my daughter, and I know what this circle is asking me to hold alongside that. Whatever you two decide, I'll hold it clean.

speaker: a004
text: Fina, Eron — I've said my piece twice and I'll say it once more because the room is still waiting: say yes or say no, and if you need a moment to speak without every eye on you, I'll clear the room and hold the door myself.
